title: Causal Asymmetry Of Classical And Quantum Autonomous Agents
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 September 2026;
tldr: This paper explores causal asymmetry in classical and quantum autonomous agents, revealing fundamental differences in how past and future constraints affect information processing.
motivation: The goal is to understand the physical limits on autonomous agents that process information, and whether quantum mechanics provides advantages over classical frameworks in terms of causal inference and thermodynamic efficiency.
method: The authors develop a formal framework for modeling autonomous agents as stochastic or quantum processes, using information-theoretic measures to quantify causal asymmetry and compare classical vs. quantum implementations.
result: They demonstrate that quantum agents can exhibit distinct causal asymmetry profiles relative to classical agents, leading to a trade-off between predictive accuracy and thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The findings highlight the deep connection between quantum information and thermodynamics, suggesting that quantum resources could enable more efficient autonomous agents.

title: Intermodal Quantum Key Distribution Over An 18-km Free-space Channel With Adaptive Optics And Room-temperature Detectors
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 August 2026;

method: The experiment employed adaptive optics to compensate for atmospheric wavefront distortions and used room-temperature detectors, likely encoding information in multiple spatial modes for intermodal QKD.

conclusion: The results highlight a promising path toward scalable, robust free-space quantum communication networks without the need for cryogenic detectors.
